studies.title: Development and initial content validation of the Vienna post-exertional malaise questionnaire: an iterative mixed-methods study.
studies.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
studies.authors: Pimminger, Theresa, Ahrens-Schwabe, Annika, Fragner, Tobias, Brandl, Tobias et al.
studies.abstract: Post-exertional malaise (PEM) is a multidimensional exertion-response pattern involving diverse triggers, variable onset, and prolonged recovery. This study developed and content-validated the Vienna Post-Exertional Malaise (VPEM) Questionnaire, a patient-reported outcome measure assessing functional decline, recovery, crash-associated symptoms, and pacing adaptations in ME/CFS. An iterative mixed-methods instrument-development study combined quantitative ratings and qualitative feedback across sequential evaluation cycles. An initial 13-item draft, informed by existing PEM, fatigue, and functional-capacity instruments and consensus literature, was evaluated by individuals with ME/CFS or Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) using Likert ratings, open-ended feedback, and interviews. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively, and qualitative data were analysed using deductive-inductive structuring content analysis. Revisions were documented in revision matrices. The revised instrument was evaluated by an interdisciplinary expert panel using domain-level and item-level ratings of relevance and clarity. Twelve individuals with ME/CFS and one individual with PCS fulfilling ME/CFS criteria evaluated the questionnaire. Ratings showed high approval for length (92.3%) and terminology (76.9%), while completeness and clarity were more heterogeneous. Qualitative findings identified ambiguities in distinguishing PEM from non-specific fatigue, missing trigger domains, and insufficient representation of intra-individual variability. After revision, the expert panel (n = 11) rated PEM coverage as complete or largely complete (100%) and the multidimensional structure as suitable or very suitable (90.9%). Item-level ratings showed high relevance (S-CVI/Ave = 0.96), whereas clarity ratings were more variable (S-CVI/Ave = 0.82). The VPEM Questionnaire operationalises PEM as multidimensional post-exertional deterioration. Findings support initial content and face validity, warranting further psychometric validation.

studies.title: A New Outlook on Infection-Associated Chronic Conditions and Illnesses.
studies.authors: Bertolli, Jeanne, Hinckley, Alison F, Mead, Paul S, Patel, Pragna et al.
studies.abstract: Infection-associated chronic conditions and illnesses (IACCI) encompass several debilitating syndromes with overlapping symptoms that have been identified and documented for decades, primarily following infectious disease outbreaks. Conditions following infection that are diagnosed with objective clinical tests have been relatively well characterized and accepted by the medical establishment, although the relationship to infection can be challenging to establish. In contrast, syndromes that lack objective tests, even when following a recognized infection, such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome, and dysautonomia, are underrecognized and often stigmatized. The COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent recognition of Long COVID as the newest example of IACCI offer new opportunities to address all aspects of IACCI. Lessons learned from the government's multi-agency public health response to Long COVID could be beneficial to ensure readiness for the long-term consequences of sporadic infections, outbreaks, and future pandemics.

studies.title: Fibromyalgia, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, and Multiple Sclerosis are associated with lower translocator protein binding affinity genotypes.
studies.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
studies.authors: Jones, Chloe, Younger, Jarred
studies.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a known pathophysiologic mechanism in multiple sclerosis and a proposed mechanism in fibromyalgia and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the translocator protein (TSPO) has been widely used to measure neuroinflammation, though second-generation ligands are highly sensitive to a single nucleotide polymorphism, rs6971, resulting in high, mixed, and low affinity binders. It is unknown whether this polymorphism is associated with neuroinflammatory disorders. Eighty-six total participant genotypes for TSPO binding affinity were identified through Sanger sequencing (30 fibromyalgia, 21 ME/CFS, 11 multiple sclerosis, and 24 healthy controls). Associations between patient group and genotype were assessed with Fisher's Exact test. Associations between genotype and symptom severity from self-report questionnaires were assessed with Kruskal-Wallis tests. In the present study individuals with fibromyalgia, (ME/CFS), or multiple sclerosis were more likely to have a mixed- or low-affinity genotypes compared to healthy controls. Presence of the low or mixed genotypes were also associated with greater self-reported fatigue severity and depressive symptoms. These findings should be confirmed in larger samples but suggest functional consequences of rs6971 polymorphism that may be related to the pathophysiology of pain and fatigue illnesses.

studies.title: More common than we thought: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, comorbidity burden, and long COVID risk in a national cohort.
studies.authors: Pearson, Megan L, Laraway, Bryan J, Elias, Ellen R, Bilousova, Ganna et al.
studies.abstract: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS) is a complex, underdiagnosed connective tissue disorder characterized by widespread symptoms affecting multiple organ systems. Recent clinical observations suggest that individuals with hEDS may be at increased risk for persistent symptoms following COVID-19, commonly referred to as Long COVID. Using data from over 19 million patients across the United States, we examined associations between hEDS, COVID-19 infection, Long COVID, and related chronic conditions. We identified just over 25,000 individuals with hEDS and estimated a prevalence of approximately 1 in 800, which is higher than previously recognized. Despite similar rates of COVID-19 infection between patients with hEDS and matched controls, patients with hEDS were nearly three times more likely to develop Long COVID. This risk was concentrated among patients with hEDS who also had overlapping conditions commonly seen in post-viral syndromes, including autonomic dysfunction (POTS), immune dysregulation (MCAS), and chronic fatigue (ME/CFS). Patients with hEDS also exhibited higher odds of having additional risk factors for severe or prolonged illness, including chronic lung and autoimmune conditions, depression, and cerebrovascular disease. A subgroup of patients received their hEDS diagnosis only after a COVID-19 or Long COVID diagnosis, and this subgroup was highly enriched for multimorbidity, particularly POTS and MCAS. These findings establish hEDS as more prevalent than previously recognized and identify a substantially elevated, comorbidity-driven risk of Long COVID in this population. Improved screening, earlier diagnosis, and integrated care pathways are urgently needed to support this complex and underserved patient group.

studies.title: A Woman With Multiple Neuropathic Symptoms, Hypersensitivity to Heat, Peppers, and Alcohol, With a Variant in the TRPV1 Capsaicin Receptor Gene: Possible Implications to ME/CFS.
studies.authors: Zimmermann, Phillip M, Boles, Richard G
studies.abstract: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is a ligand and heat-gated ion channel expressed on nociceptors that plays a central role in thermal and chemical pain signaling. Loss-of-function variants in TRPV1 have been associated with reduced nociception. We report a 65-year-old woman with disabling polyneurofunctional/neuropathic symptomatology including migraine, functional gastrointestinal disorders, and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Diagnostic evaluation revealed sensory polyneuropathy and autonomic instability. Whole genome sequencing reanalysis identified a heterozygous TRPV1 c.2174A > T (p.Lys725Met) Likely Pathogenic variant that is very rare and highly conserved. Our patient reports consistent, longstanding, marked hypersensitivity to heat, capsaicin, and alcohol, all of which are known TRPV1 agonists, supporting a gain-of-function mechanism for this variant. Furthermore, prior studies have implicated TRPV1 hyperactivity in migraine, nociceptive sensitization, and ME/CFS. Despite the excellent clinical correlation, causality of the variant cannot be definitively established without functional studies. This case expands the potential phenotypic spectrum associated with TRPV1, and highlights a possible role for TRPV1-mediated channelopathies in complex neurofunctional disorders including ME/CFS.

studies.title: Symptom clusters and symptom network characteristics in chronic fatigue syndrome patients: a cross-sectional study.
studies.authors: Zi, Aiqun, Zhang, Yihan, Sun, Min, Liu, Ting et al.
studies.abstract: Chronic fatigue syndrome is characterized by multiple co-occurring physical, cognitive, sleep, and emotional symptoms. Traditional symptom cluster analysis identifies patterns of symptom co-occurrence but does not clarify the relative importance of individual symptoms or the connections between symptom clusters. Symptom network analysis may complement this approach by identifying core and bridge symptoms. To investigate the symptom clusters and structural characteristics of symptom networks in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome, thereby providing a basis for developing targeted strategies for managing symptoms. A convenience sampling method was used to enroll 214 patients with chronic fatigue syndrome. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and an adapted version of the Chinese Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale. Data were analyzed using SPSS 27.0. Symptom clusters were extracted using principal component analysis (PCA) with varimax rotation, and a symptom network was constructed in R to calculate expected influence and bridge expected influence, thereby identifying core and bridge symptoms. The three most common symptoms, in descending order, were fatigue (100.00%), difficulty concentrating (90.7%), and feeling drowsy (86.9%). A total of six symptom clusters were identified: Emotional-Sleep Symptom cluster, Fatigue Symptom cluster, Physical symptom cluster, Self-Image symptom cluster, Gastrointestinal symptom cluster, and Neurological symptom cluster, with a cumulative variance contribution of 63.114%. Fatigue had the highest expected influence (rEI = 1.541), followed by worrying (rEI = 1.169); fatigue (rbEI = 0.430), pain (rbEI = 0.363), and difficulty sleeping (rbEI = 0.309) were the primary bridge symptoms. Patients with chronic fatigue syndrome exhibit co-occurring symptoms and connections across symptom clusters. Fatigue serves as both a core symptom and a bridging symptom, while worrying, difficulty sleeping, and pain are also critical areas of focus in symptom management. Clinically, fatigue should be prioritized for assessment and management, while concurrently conducting comprehensive evaluations of mood, sleep, and pain. Individualized management plans should be developed based on the characteristics of symptom clusters and symptom networks to alleviate the symptom burden in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome and improve their quality of life.

studies.title: Outcome measures in long COVID clinical trials: a review.
studies.authors: van Rhijn-Brouwer, Femke C C, de Canson, Chloé, VanDerNagel, Joanneke E L, Westerhuis, Xandra et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a multisystem disease that affects approximately 10% of people after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. In the absence of curative treatment, high-quality clinical treatment trials are urgently needed for long COVID. There is significant overlap between long COVID and other infection-associated chronic conditions, in particular myalgic encephalomyelitis. As such, trial design for long COVID can benefit from prior experience in this field. In this review we explore outcome measures in long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis clinical trials to survey current practices, and provide recommendations for future clinical trials. PubMed and Clinicaltrials.gov were searched for clinical trials on long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis that featured a biomedical intervention. 37 myalgic encephalomyelitis and 68 long COVID trials were identified that used 397 outcome measures in total. We then critically assessed the relevance of these outcome measures for patients. Long COVID trial design could be improved by incorporating outcomes that address important symptom clusters such as post-exertional malaise, dysautonomia and mast cell activation. Clinical assessments, physical tests and biomarkers can supplement patient reported outcome measure data, if safety, feasibility and applicability are carefully considered. Lastly, safety of the intervention is rarely adequately evaluated. We recommend a concerted effort to include patient input at all steps of clinical trial design, execution and evaluation.

studies.title: More pronounced diurnal cortisol rhythms are longitudinally associated with less fatigue in colorectal cancer survivors: A 12-month prospective cohort study.
studies.authors: Frenken, Koen G, Scheer, Frank A J L, Qian, Jingyi, Bours, Martijn J L et al.
studies.abstract: Fatigue is amongst the most debilitating cancer-related symptoms, affecting up to one-third of colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors. Accumulating evidence implicates dysregulation of HPA axis as a potential mechanism contributing to chronic fatigue syndrome. We examined longitudinal associations between parameters of diurnal cortisol rhythms and fatigue in CRC survivors up to 12 months after treatment. Seventy-four survivors of CRC were assessed at 6 weeks, 6 months and 12 months after treatment. At each point, salivary samples were collected five times per day over two consecutive days to measure cortisol concentrations. Relative amplitude (RA), diurnal slope, area under the curve (AUCg) and cortisol awakening response (CAR) were derived as a comprehensive assessment of diurnal cortisol rhythms. Fatigue was assessed at all time points using the Checklist Individual Strength (CIS; range overall score: 20-140; motivational subscale: 4-28) and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 (EORTC; range: 0-100). Longitudinal associations were analyzed using confounder-adjusted linear mixed models, with coefficients (β) indicating differences in fatigue scores over time per SD increase in cortisol parameters. A higher RA was associated with less overall fatigue (EORTC: β= -1.42; 95%CI: -2.82, -0.03; CIS: β= -1.82; 95%CI: -3.63, -0.01). A flatter diurnal slope, indicating less decline in cortisol over the day, was associated with more fatigue (EORTC: β=1.64; 0.25, 3.03) and increased motivational fatigue (CIS: β= 0.45; 0.02, 0.88). More pronounced diurnal cortisol rhythms, specifically a higher RA and steeper diurnal slope, were longitudinally associated with less fatigue in CRC survivors. These findings may suggest that improving 24-h cortisol rhythmicity could be a target for interventions to reduce fatigue in CRC survivors, but this warrants further investigations.

studies.title: Stress-inducible WASF3 regulates brain metabolism and cognitive function.
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
studies.authors: Syed, Abu M, Ma, Jin, Wang, Ping-Yuan, Son, Youlim et al.
studies.abstract: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein family member 3 (WASF3) disrupts mitochondrial respiration and is induced in association with endoplasmic reticulum stress in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Because cognitive impairment is a hallmark of ME/CFS, we investigated the role of WASF3 in brain metabolism and function using WASF3 transgenic and knockout mouse models. WASF3 disrupted respiratory complex IV and localized to mitochondria-associated membranes, known to modulate cellular processes important for neuronal activity. Overexpression of WASF3 in the hippocampus, a critical region for memory formation, induced a metabolic shift toward glycolysis and promoted a "hypometabolic" state. Increased WASF3 also caused a reduction in ATPIF1, previously shown to facilitate cognitive function, and impaired learning. Conversely, WASF3 deficiency increased ATPIF1 level, enhanced oxidative metabolism, and preserved cognitive function under stress. Together, these findings demonstrate that WASF3 suppresses oxidative metabolism in the brain and contributes to cognitive dysfunction, providing mechanistic insights into the "brain fog" reported in ME/CFS.

studies.title: The Glymphatic-Meningeal Lymphatic System and Autophagy in ME/CFS and Long COVID: A Mechanistic Perspective.
studies.authors: Nemat-Gorgani, Mohsen, Jensen, Michael Anthony, Davis, Ronald Wayne
studies.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Long COVID) are complex multisystem disorders affecting 60-400 million individuals globally. They are considered post-infectious illnesses and share similar biological mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, orthostatic intolerance and cognitive dysfunction, highlighting a substantial overlap between the two conditions. Persistent fatigue, sleep dysfunction, post-exertional malaise and brain fog are among some of their most common and debilitating symptoms. Despite extensive research, they remain incurable, with no effective treatments, or simple diagnostic tests. They are increasingly understood as heterogeneous, multisystem diseases, involving neurological symptoms, with varying severities and diverse underlying biological abnormalities. More recently, the possibility of glymphatic dysfunction and autophagy impairment have been proposed as parts of the mechanistic features of the pathophysiology of these conditions, which are discussed more fully in the present perspective. With the glymphatic and meningeal lymphatic systems being operationally integrated, we will try to delineate how the metabolic waste removal mechanism afforded by this system may work together with autophagy to maintain brain homeostasis. We will provide some of the established mechanistic features of toxicity of misfolded proteins, explore their role in causing glymphatic dysfunction and impairing autophagy, and discuss the potential for therapeutic interventions.

studies.title: CATCH-EVseq, an Ultra-Sensitive Capture Assay to Monitor Human Enterovirus RNA.
studies.authors: Germain, Arnaud, Hanson, Maureen R
studies.abstract: The detection of low-abundance viral RNA in chronic or persistent infections remains a major challenge in virology, constrained by the sensitivity and specificity of traditional methods. One such infection, chronic enterovirus (EV) infection, has been proposed as a potential underlying factor in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME), although this hypothesis remains debated. Supporting evidence for EVs as a viral trigger includes historical spatiotemporal overlaps between ME outbreaks and poliomyelitis epidemics, frequent reports of "flu-like" illness at disease onset, seasonal outbreaks patterns, and serological findings. To address the problem of EV detection, we developed CATCH-EVseq, an ultra-sensitive platform built on the CATCH framework. By integrating high-throughput sequencing with cDNA capture using 49,847 probes targeting 3410 EV genomes, CATCH-EVseq achieved a detection limit in artificially created samples as low as one copy in a microgram of RNA for two out of three biological replicates. Additionally, spike-in controls allow for rigorous validation of the capture and sequencing throughout the CATCH-EVseq procedure. When applied to a small number of blood samples from both ME patients and healthy controls, CATCH-EVseq detected no EV RNA, either in direct assays or after in vitro viral amplification. While these results do not support the presence of circulating EV RNA in the blood of individuals with ME, they do not rule out persistent infection in other tissues or organs. Critically, CATCH-EVseq establishes a robust, ultra-sensitive framework for future investigations of low-level EV persistence in biopsies, post-mortem tissues, or other clinical contexts where chronic enterovirus infection is suspected.

studies.title: ME/CFS and the thalamus as a precision gate: what reversible thalamocortical connectivity reveals about central gain in post-infectious fatigue.
studies.authors: Strube, Andreas
studies.abstract: Kim and colleagues report a finding that is easy to understate: thalamic hyperconnectivity with sensorimotor and visuo-occipital cortices, present in patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) at baseline, shifts back toward the pattern seen in healthy controls after hyperbaric oxygen therapy and does so most in the patients who improve clinically. To my knowledge, this is the first treatment-coupled, apparently reversible thalamocortical signature in ME/CFS. Viewed through predictive processing (the framework in which the brain continually predicts its own sensory and bodily inputs), the thalamus is theorised to be a gain-control gate that helps set the precision or weight assigned to ascending bodily signals. I argue that the baseline hyperconnectivity reflects deficient filtering of expected input, and that its post-treatment reduction may index restored filtering. The same failure of attenuation offers a parsimonious account of several symptoms that often co-occur in patients, including sensory hypersensitivity, pain, orthostatic intolerance, and cognitive "brain fog", as one mechanism expressed across exteroceptive, nociceptive, autonomic, and cognitive domains. Because hyperbaric oxygen therapy is a vascular intervention and resting-state connectivity is an indirect measure this gain interpretation remains a hypothesis and I outline how it can be tested across exertion and post-exertional malaise rather than at baseline alone.

studies.title: Overlapping Post-COVID Conditions: A Case of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome Triggered by Sequential Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Infections.
studies.authors: Mayrink Magalhães, Virgínia R, Ribeiro Oliveira, Laura A, Lourenço, Adelina J, Ribeiro Camargos, Isabela et al.
studies.abstract: The rise in post-infectious syndromes following COVID-19, such as Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), has become increasingly common in clinical practice, representing an emerging clinical challenge. This case highlights a possible clinical scenario involving the interaction between sequential viral infections - such as the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) - in triggering overlapping chronic conditions. This report presents the case of a patient who developed ME/CFS and POTS following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a prior history of EBV mononucleosis, and discusses the diagnostic, therapeutic, and pathophysiological implications. A 48-year-old woman with a history of mononucleosis in childhood developed persistent and disabling symptoms after COVID-19 in January 2022. She presented with extreme fatigue, orthostatic intolerance, paresthesia, cognitive dysfunction, and multisystem symptoms. After extensive investigation, she was diagnosed with ME/CFS (early 2023) and POTS (later that year). Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) was considered as a hypothesis during follow-up, but objective testing was not confirmatory. Management included pharmacological therapy (including low-dose naltrexone, duloxetine, and palmitoylethanolamide (PEA)), activity adjustments (pacing), and a multidisciplinary approach, with partial and fluctuating responses. This case illustrates how viral infections such as EBV and SARS-CoV-2 may act as sequential triggers in an individual clinical trajectory compatible with the development of ME/CFS and POTS. The symptomatic overlap, the lack of readily available objective biomarkers in this patient, and the need for a predominantly clinical and functional diagnostic approach in her evaluation highlight the complexity of these conditions. This experience also underscores the importance of continued efforts in research, clinical training, and integrated care models to improve the management of patients presenting with post-COVID conditions (PCC).

studies.title: Transient clinical improvement and immune modulation following recombinant Zoster vaccination in a patient with ME/CFS.
studies.authors: Bigleri, AmirAli, Alimo, Emmanuel T, Abouda, Amal, Osman, Mohammed et al.
studies.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a debilitating multisystem disorder associated with immune dysregulation yet lacks definitive biomarkers or effective therapies. Acute immune perturbations may transiently modulate disease manifestations. We report the case of a female patient in her 60s with severe, long-standing ME/CFS who experienced changes in symptom following administration of recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed pre- and post-vaccination using flow cytometry, with comparison to a female healthy control. Plasma galectin-9 (Gal-9) levels were quantified by ELISA. Both RZV doses were associated with rapid, transient remission of symptoms, including improved sleep, cognition, pain, mobility, and respiratory function, followed by relapse. Immunologically, pre-vaccination profiling revealed elevated monocytes, increased CD71 This case demonstrates that immune stimulation via RZV may transiently reverse immune dysfunction and improve clinical symptoms in ME/CFS. These findings support a role for reversible immune exhaustion in disease pathogenesis and highlight potential avenues for biomarker development and therapeutic intervention.

studies.title: Construction and verification of an immune signature model for chronic fatigue syndrome: Leveraging TCM syndromes and elements for enhanced assessment.
studies.authors: Qin, Le-le, Zhang, Zhen-Xian, Wang, Jing-Han, Shi, Jia-Ning et al.
studies.abstract: The purpose of this study is to establish an immune function assessment model that considers clinical symptoms and laboratory tests by combining traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndromes and syndrome elements with lymphocyte cell counts for evaluating immune function in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS). A survey was conducted involving 473 CFS patients who were categorized based on immune function and divided into training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. Logistic analyses were performed on clinical data, leading to a nomogram model whose discrimination and sensitivity were assessed, along with clinical applicability via decision curve analysis. Among the 473 CFS patients, 225 (47.6%) had weakened immune function. Multivariate logistic regression identified CD4 Our CFS immune function evaluation model combines TCM syndromes and elements and shows predictive value and clinical applicability. Please cite this article as: Qin LL, Zhang ZX, Wang JH, Shi JN, Shao X, Yang F, Chen M, Jiang TJ, Ge WJ. studies.title: Beyond the pelvis: redefining endometriosis as a systemic inflammatory disorder. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
studies.authors: Zheng, Sai-Hua, Gao, Shao-Jun, Cai, Jing-Jing, Shen, Zong-Xiang et al.
studies.abstract: Endometriosis has traditionally been defined as a disease localized to the pelvis. However, its clinical presentation is often accompanied by systemic comorbidities that extend far beyond the pelvic cavity, a phenomenon that challenges the traditional disease paradigm. This study aimed to comprehensively assess the associations between endometriosis and autoimmune diseases, allergic conditions, chronic pain syndromes, and endocrine disorders through a systematic review and meta-analysis, thereby providing evidence for redefining endometriosis as a systemic immuno-inflammatory disorder. To conduct this study, a comprehensive search strategy was employed to identify relevant published studies. Electronic databases, including Web of Science and Medline, were searched from their inception up to December 31, 2025. We additionally examined the reference lists of all identified papers to capture any additional articles that were not identified through the electronic database searches. Eligible studies were observational in design (cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional) and reported quantitative data on the association between endometriosis and predefined comorbidities in women. Exclusion criteria included non-human studies, non-English publications, secondary literature types (e.g., reviews, case reports), and studies lacking sufficient data for effect size calculation. Quality assessment was conducted based on the GRADE criteria. The final analysis included 55 studies that met the predefined inclusion criteria and were incorporated into the comprehensive analysis. Of these, 48 studies provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis (meta-analysis). Specifically, 32 studies investigated the association between endometriosis and autoimmune diseases: 14 on systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), 8 on Sjögren's syndrome (SS), 10 on rheumatoid arthritis (RA), 5 on multiple sclerosis (MS), 5 on celiac disease (CLD), and 4 on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Additionally, 17 studies examined associations with allergic diseases, 13 focused on pain syndromes, and 6 explored associations with endocrine disorders. Meta-analysis showed that women with endometriosis had a significantly higher risk of certain autoimmune diseases in cohort studies, including SLE (RR: 1.81, 95% CI: 1.50-2.18), SS (RR: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.40-1.71), and RA (RR: 1.71, 95% CI: 1.40-2.09), as well as significantly higher odds in case-control and cross-sectional studies for SLE (OR: 3.93, 95% CI: 2.59-5.98), SS (OR: 3.13, 95% CI: 1.10-8.90), RA (OR: 2.27, 95% CI: 1.75-2.95), MS (OR: 2.30, 95% CI: 1.57-3.37), CLD (OR: 4.50, 95% CI: 1.94-10.42), and IBD (OR: 2.82, 95% CI: 0.58-13.61). Significant associations were also observed for allergic conditions-such as asthma (RR: 1.27, 95% CI: 1.14-1.40) and eczema (OR: 1.58, 95% CI: 1.34-1.87)-and for pain syndromes including fibromyalgia (RR: 1.65, 95% CI: 1.42-1.92), chronic fatigue syndrome (RR: 1.41, 95% CI: 1.31-1.51), and irritable bowel syndrome (RR: 2.51, 95% CI: 1.55-4.07; OR: 3.49, 95% CI: 3.21-3.80). In contrast, no statistically significant increase was observed in the odds of endocrine disorders such as hypothyroidism (OR: 1.89, 95% CI: 0.61-5.90) and hyperthyroidism (OR: 0.95, 95% CI: 0.60-1.52) among women with endometriosis compared with women without endometriosis. However, the overall quality of evidence was generally low or very low according to the GRADE approach, largely due to a high risk of bias in most of the included study designs and statistical analyses. The body of evidence provided by this study supports the reconceptualization of endometriosis as a systemic immuno-inflammatory disease. The associations with various comorbidities are underpinned by shared mechanisms of immune dysregulation and central sensitization. This paradigm shift necessitates a move in clinical practice from a purely gynecological intervention model toward a patient-centered, comprehensive multidisciplinary management approach. It also provides a theoretical foundation for developing novel treatment strategies targeting shared pathological pathways. CRD420251258716.

studies.title: [Recognizing and managing post-exertional malaise in primary care].
studies.authors: Garcia, Sara, Tzartzas, Konstantinos, von Plessen, Christian, Favrat, Bernard et al.
studies.abstract: Post-exertional malaise (PEM) is a syndrome characterized by a worsening of symptoms after physical, cognitive, or emotional exertion. It presents as increased fatigue, usually accompanied by other clinical symptoms, such as muscle pain or cognitive impairment. First described in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME), PEM is now recognized as a hallmark of post-infectious syndromes that have received increasing attention through the emergence of long COVID. PEM is a distinguishing symptom of these conditions, and its early detection and appropriate management are essential to prevent long-term functional decline of affected patients. This review describes the definition and clinical impact of PEM and summarizes current recommendations for its management. Le malaise post-effort (MPE) est un syndrome d’aggravation de symptômes à la suite d’un effort physique, cognitif, social ou émotionnel. Il se manifeste par une péjoration de la fatigue associée à d’autres symptômes, comme des douleurs musculaires ou des troubles cognitifs. Initialement décrit chez les personnes atteintes du syndrome de fatigue chronique/encéphalomyélite myalgique (SFC/EM), le MPE se retrouve également dans les syndromes postinfectieux mis en lumière par l’émergence du Covid long. La détection précoce du MPE, symptôme discriminant de ces pathologies, et sa prise en charge adéquate sont fondamentales afin d’améliorer le pronostic et d’éviter la détérioration de l’état fonctionnel des patients concernés. Cet article vise à détailler la définition, l’impact clinique et les stratégies de gestion du MPE.

studies.title: The impact of creatine on brain functions.
studies.authors: Borowski, Tymoteusz, Zimoń, Maria, Piegza, Magdalena Justyna
studies.abstract: As an endogenous compound essential for energy homeostasis, creatine holds a fundamental role in the bioenergetics of the brain, an organ with high metabolic requirements. This review provides a synthesis of current knowledge on the impact of creatine on the functions of the central nervous system (CNS). The brain, which is capable of de novo creatine synthesis, demonstrates an increase in its internal concentrations following supplementation; however, this effect is less significant than in muscle tissue and is constrained by the blood-brain barrier, among other factors. The development of effective CNS-targeted dosing strategies remains a subject of ongoing research. An overview of the literature suggests that creatine supplementation may beneficially influence cognitive performance, particularly under conditions of elevated metabolic demand like stress or sleep deprivation, with the potential to enhance memory and mitigate fatigue. Nonetheless, findings from the cited research are inconsistent due to methodological heterogeneity and a common failure to directly measure brain creatine levels. Reports on creatine's antidepressant properties are particularly encouraging, with preclinical and initial clinical studies pointing to its potential utility (e.g., via the mTORC1 pathway) in augmenting mood disorder treatments. Moreover, the authors examine the use of creatine in chronic fatigue syndrome, where evidence supports improvements in physical performance and reductions in pain intensity, although its effect on generalized fatigue remains ambiguous.

studies.title: Identification of SGK1 as a candidate regulator associated with myeloid cell senescence in ME/CFS: An integrative transcriptomic and experimental study.
studies.authors: Jin, Yan, Qin, Rui, Li, Wan, Liu, Jin et al.
studies.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex illness lacking objective diagnostic biomarkers and clear pathophysiological understanding. Patients exhibit immune dysregulation and chronic inflammation reminiscent of aging phenotypes, yet the role of myeloid cell senescence in this disease remains unexplored. A stepwise integrative transcriptomic and computational strategy was employed. Differentially expressed genes were identified from the bulk transcriptomic dataset GSE14577. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis was performed to identify key modules correlated with the ME/CFS phenotype. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting these modules with aging-related genes from the GenAge database. Core hub genes were further selected using LASSO regression and random forest machine learning algorithms. Cell type-specific expression was mapped using single-cell RNA sequencing data GSE214283, and functional validation was conducted via siRNA knockdown in a THP-1 cell senescence model. Integrative analysis identified HMGCR and SGK1 as core hub genes. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that candidate genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular senescence and inflammation. Single-cell transcriptomics analysis suggested that SGK1 expression was enriched in myeloid cell populations, including monocytes and neutrophils, in individuals with ME/CFS, whereas HMGCR showed a broader expression pattern. Single-gene GSEA indicated that SGK1 was associated with autophagy and lysosomal function. In vitro experiments showed that SGK1 expression was significantly upregulated in D-galactose-induced senescent THP-1 cells, and SGK1 knockdown markedly reduced the mRNA expression levels of senescence markers p16, p21, and p53. This study identifies SGK1 as a candidate molecule associated with myeloid cell senescence-related alterations in ME/CFS. Integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses suggest a potential link between SGK1 expression and aging-associated immune alterations. However, further validation in primary ME/CFS-derived immune cells and clinical cohorts is required to determine the biological significance and clinical relevance of SGK1.

studies.title: [An insight into the long/post COVID care situation in Germany-a rapid scoping review].
studies.authors: Ebster, Marlene, Gscheidle, Sonja, Lange, Saskia, Weijburg, Thomas et al.
studies.abstract: Long/post COVID and related conditions such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and post-vaccination syndrome are associated with persistent functional impairments and are met with care structures in Germany that are difficult to navigate. The rapid scoping review offers an insight into care structures, capacities, access, care pathways and gaps in care for these patient groups in the German healthcare system. It also takes into account patient and care provider perspectives. The study follows the recommendations of the Joanna Briggs Institute and the PRISMA ScR checklist for conducting (rapid) scoping reviews. A MEDLINE search was conducted from 2020 onwards with predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria for evidence sources related to care in Germany. 44 evidence sources were included. General practitioners and paediatricians act as the first point of contact. Specialised outpatient clinics and rehabilitation facilities take on complex diagnostics and patient treatment. Care networks are rare. Navigating the healthcare system is characterised by information gaps, unclear responsibilities and long waiting times, so that those affected often organise their own care. Some report stigmatisation, misdiagnoses and stressful activation recommendations despite the risk of post exertional malaise. Care is unevenly accessible, poorly coordinated and only limitedly evidence based. Shared knowledge and case databases, training, better diagnostic tools and robust efficacy studies are needed to improve access, management and safety of long/post COVID care. HINTERGRUND: Long/Post COVID und verwandte Krankheitsbilder wie Myalgische Enzephalomyelitis/Chronisches Fatigue Syndrom, Posturales Orthostatisches Tachykardiesyndrom (POTS) und Postvakzinierungssyndrom gehen mit anhaltenden Funktionseinschränkungen einher und treffen auf schwer überschaubare Versorgungsstrukturen. ZIEL: Der Rapid Scoping Review bietet einen Einblick in Versorgungsstrukturen, Kapazitäten, Zugänge und Versorgungslücken für diese Patientengruppen im deutschen Gesundheitssystem. Dabei werden auch die Perspektiven von Leistungserbringenden und Betroffenen berücksichtigt. Die Arbeit folgt den Empfehlungen des Joanna Briggs Institute und der PRISMA-ScR-Checkliste zur Durchführung von (Rapid) Scoping Reviews. Es erfolgte eine MEDLINE-Suche ab 2020 mit vordefinierten Ein- und Ausschlusskriterien für Evidenzquellen mit Bezug zur Versorgung in Deutschland. Es wurden 44 Quellen eingeschlossen. Haus- und kinderärztliche Praxen fungieren als erste Anlaufstelle. Spezialisierte Ambulanzen und Rehabilitationseinrichtungen übernehmen komplexe Diagnostik und Patientenbehandlung. Versorgungsnetzwerke sind selten. Die Navigation von Betroffenen durch das Gesundheitswesen ist von Informationslücken, unklaren Zuständigkeiten und langen Wartezeiten geprägt, sodass diese ihre Versorgung häufig selbst organisieren. Betroffene berichten teilweise von Stigmatisierung, Fehldiagnosen und belastenden Aktivierungsempfehlungen trotz des Risikos einer Post-Exertionellen Malaise. Die Versorgung ist ungleich zugänglich, wenig koordiniert und nur begrenzt evidenzbasiert. Gemeinsame Wissens- und Falldatenbanken, Fortbildungen, bessere diagnostische Instrumente und robuste Wirksamkeitsstudien sind erforderlich, um Zugang, Steuerung und Sicherheit der Long/Post COVID-Versorgung zu verbessern.

studies.title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) are associated with distinct clinical phenotypes two years after SARS-CoV-2 infection: A data-driven approach.
studies.authors: Verfaillie, Sander C J, Verveen, Anouk, Visser, Denise, Nieuwkerk, Pythia et al.
studies.abstract: It is important to determine whether the persistent cognitive and fatigue complaints, as part of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), are associated with underlying patterns and specific symptoms clusters. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate symptom clusters and clinical phenotypes in PASC. We included n = 153 individuals (53 years old, 66% female, 2 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection) categorized into groups with (n = 88) and without (n = 65) PASC, defined by severe fatigue and concentration problems using validated cut-offs. Symptom clusters (i.e., component loadings and component scores) were identified using principal component analyses (PCA, eigenvalue[EV]>1.0), using clinical, somatic, coping and sleep factors, symptom severity, neuropsychological and physical tests (totalling 19 tests and questionnaires). We then used logistic regression techniques on (participant-level) component scores (standardized) to investigate associations with PASC. Finally, K-means clustering methods to identify clinical phenotypes. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, education, nationality and time since infection. PCA identified 5 components, explaining 70% of the variance. We labelled these components as follows: (1) PEM, ME/CFS and sleep symptoms, coping factors (EV = 7.0, 36.9% variance), (2) information-processing speed (EV = 2.5, 13.3%), (3) executive functioning (EV = 1.5, 8.0%, (4) physical performance (EV = 1.2, 6.5%), (5) somatic comorbidities and hospital admission (EV = 1.0, 5.5%). Logistic regression showed that only the first component scores (Odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 97.1 [16.5-570.3], p < 0.001,), and none of the others (all p > 0.05), associated with PASC. Cluster analysis revealed two distinct clinical phenotypes among individuals with severe chronic fatigue: one marked by physical impairment and the other by diminished cognitive performance. Consistent with existing literature, we confirmed that PASC is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by extensive, interrelated symptoms. Notably, we identified specific cognitive and physical clinical phenotypes. These findings are important for future targeted diagnosis and treatment.

studies.title: Measures of Overall Illness Severity and Burden for ME/CFS: A Scoping Review.
studies.authors: Cripe, Jada, Ravichandran, Suvetha, Deditz, Samantha, Jason, Leonard A
studies.abstract: Consensus has not been established on measures of illness severity and burden for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS), which is characterized by a wide range of symptoms including post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, and cognitive impairment. A scoping review was conducted to systematically evaluate the measurement of illness severity and burden in individuals with ME/CFS. A literature search was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines across five academic databases and one patient-organization-led website (with no restrictions on publication date; restricted to English language studies, and excluding review articles). Records were imported into Covidence, a systematic and scoping review data management tool, with studies retained if they evaluated an ME/CFS population and explicitly measured illness severity or illness burden. Information from each source was extracted and relevant measures were evaluated. From the reviewed literature, 190 full-text articles met the final inclusion criteria and were retained for analysis. The most frequently utilized tools for evaluating illness severity and burden in individuals with ME/CFS were the Medical Outcomes Study 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36) and the Sickness Impact Profile (SIP). Additional prominent instruments identified across the literature include disease-specific measures such as the DePaul Symptom Questionnaire (DSQ) and generic health-related quality of life indices like the EuroQoL 5-Dimension (EQ-5D-5L). Significant discrepancies persist in how illness severity and illness burden are operationalized in ME/CFS research. The reliance on generic instruments often obscures core symptom domains like post-exertional malaise (PEM), while inconsistent standards limit cross-comparability. Establishing standardized, disease-specific illness metrics is critical to accurately capturing the true burden of illness and advancing rigorous clinical research.

studies.title: Facilitators and barriers to decentralized Long COVID platform clinical trials using repurposed drugs.
studies.authors: Schito, Marco, Coe, Stacey, Seltzer, Jaime, Davis, Hannah E et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is an emerging chronic condition that results in substantial impairments in quality of life, physical function, and ability to maintain gainful employment. There are no FDA-approved treatments for Long COVID, and recent institution-based clinical trials have not yielded effective treatments. Current standard of care involves trial-and-error drug repurposing that warrants evaluation in rigorous clinical trials. Here we describe potential advantages of decentralized repurposing drug trials as an alternative or complementary approach to institution-based trials. Additionally, we describe lessons learned when launching a local feasibility pilot trial that may inform the design of future decentralized trials in the Long COVID field.

studies.title: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: a critical narrative review of modern concepts and unani perspectives.
studies.authors: Israr, Ishrat Mohammed, Eram, Faseeha, Ahmed, Md Mujahid
studies.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a chronic, disabling, multisystem illness characterized by persistent fatigue, post-exertional malaise/post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PEM/PESE), unrefreshing sleep, and cognitive impairment. Classical Unani medicine does not recognize ME/CFS as a distinct disease entity. However, its descriptions of fatigue (I'yā), particularly I'yā Dhātī (spontaneous fatigue), provide a basis for examining parallels with ME/CFS. To examine I'yā Dhātī (spontaneous fatigue) and its three simple subtypes (I'yā Qarūḥī, I'yā Tamaddudī, and I'yā Waramī) and compare them qualitatively with contemporary ME/CFS, including areas of similarity and discordance. This critical narrative review used structured searches of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science. Eight primary Unani sources were examined: Al-Qānūn fi al-Ṭibb, Kulliyāt al-Qānūn, Kitāb al-Ḥāwī, Kitāb al-Murshid, Kitāb al-Manṣūrī, Dhakhīrah-i Khwārazm Shāhī, Kitāb al-Kulliyāt, and Al-Mukhtārāt fi al-Ṭibb. The three subtypes were compared using predefined qualitative domains based on contemporary ME/CFS features and classical descriptions. I'yā Tamaddudī (distensive fatigue) showed the greatest phenomenological overlap with ME/CFS, particularly spontaneous fatigue, generalized heaviness, sleep disturbances, mental dullness, reduced functional capacity, and diffuse somatic manifestations. However, no clearly documented classical equivalent of delayed PEM/PESE was identified, representing a major area of discordance. I'yā Tamaddudī (distensive fatigue) showed the greatest phenomenological/conceptual overlap with ME/CFS among the subtypes examined. This represents a historical and interpretative correspondence, not biological, diagnostic, or therapeutic equivalence. Independent operationalization and prospective evaluation are required before its clinical or biological relevance can be established.

studies.title: Temporal dynamics of the cerebrospinal fluid proteome in tick-borne encephalitis and enteroviral meningitis.
studies.authors: Morén, Jakob, Li, Peng, Bartfai, Aniko, Günther, Göran et al.
studies.abstract: Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a severe viral infection of the central nervous system (CNS), causing acute meningoencephalitis and often long-term neurocognitive sequelae. The lack of specific treatment for TBE highlights the need to improve understanding of disease mechanisms and identify novel biomarkers. Enteroviral meningitis is typically a milder infection of the CNS and rarely causes encephalitis. In this hypothesis-generating study, we aimed to characterise temporal changes in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteome in TBE and identify candidate biomarkers associated with pathophysiological mechanisms, disease severity, and neurocognitive outcome. Patients with TBE, enteroviral meningitis, or aseptic meningoencephalitis of unknown origin were retrospectively included from a previously established cohort. CSF proteomes were analysed by label-free mass spectrometry, followed by differential protein expression analysis and functional annotation. Temporal proteome dynamics and protein associations with disease severity and neurocognitive outcome were assessed. Data are available Proteomic analyses revealed alterations in proteins related to synaptic function, inflammatory pathways, the complement system, and the 14-3-3 protein family. Adrenomedullin was markedly increased in the late phase of TBE compared with enteroviral meningitis. Temporal changes in the CSF proteome in TBE indicate a strong inflammatory response occurring in concert with lower levels of proteins related to synaptic function during the acute phase. These findings provide insights into the host response and pathogenesis of TBE and identify proteins of potential interest for future validation.

studies.title: Which needs do children, adolescents, and young adults with ME/CFS and their parents express and feel? - Qualitative study in Germany.
studies.authors: Kircher, Alissa, Mayer-Huber, Sandra, Eberhartinger, Maria, Mihatsch, Lorenz et al.
studies.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex, multi-system disease that significantly deteriorates the quality of life for those affected. There is no established effective treatment, and a lack of research on what is needed by severely affected young people with ME/CFS and their caring parents to cope with the disease. The aim of this study was to investigate the needs of young people affected and their parents in order to subsequently build a tailored treatment model for this age group upon this basis. Needs were explored using topic-guided focus groups and an adapted diary method. Patients participated either in an online focus group with five sessions discussing needs related to five topics (sports/physical activity/mobility, self-care, mental activity, social contacts, and school/vocational training/study/profession) or in the adaptive diary approach, receiving and answering the same stimuli and questions in the format of voice and text messages. Additionally, focus groups with parents comprised two sessions each, targeting needs of their children and themselves, respectively. Data were analysed by reflexive thematic analysis. We included 14 young people with ME/CFS (aged 12 to 25 years), of whom five participated in a focus group and nine in the adaptive diary approach. Eighteen parents took part in three focus groups, including three couples. In the patient sample, four themes of unmet needs were identified: (i) not being left alone with the disease, (ii) flexibility and understanding of healthcare providers and authorities, (iii) having to explain oneself less to others, and (iv) appreciation of the family filling part of the healthcare gap. Among parents, the following four themes were revealed: (i) not being left alone with the disease, (ii) health care adapted to ME/CFS, (iii) knowledge, understanding, and acceptance of ME/CFS, and (iv) confidence in dealing with ME/CFS. The needs of young people with ME/CFS and their parents, respectively, overlap clearly and demonstrate the importance of a needs-based adaptation of healthcare services.

studies.title: searchMECFS: An online, interactive platform to facilitate secondary use of biospecimens and associated research data from myalgic encephalomyelitis studies.
studies.authors: Barnette, Quinn, LeGrow, Keith, Ham, Michael, Illei, Dóra et al.
studies.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex, debilitating disease affecting multiple body systems, with no established biomarkers for diagnosis or treatment. This publication introduces searchMECFS, a free, interactive online platform developed by the Data Management and Coordinating Center (DMCC) of the ME/CFS Research Network, with funding from the National Institutes of Health. The platform's purpose is to facilitate the secondary use of biospecimens and associated research data from ME/CFS clinical studies by improving accessibility, visibility, and sharing of these resources. Currently, searchMECFS facilitates access to biospecimens and associated data from two studies: The Chronic Fatigue Initiative (CFI) study funded by the Hutchins Family Foundation and the Multi-Site Clinical Assessment of ME/CFS study (MCAM) funded by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Users can query participant demographics and clinical information and request available biospecimens through an application process. Eight specimen types are currently available, although availability varies by study. The results highlight a case where a researcher used the searchMECFS platform to identify 40 serum samples, which contributed to published research on circadian rhythm disruption in ME/CFS. searchMECFS aims to accelerate scientific discovery within the ME/CFS research community by improving biospecimen utilization, fostering data sharing, and supporting collaboration.

studies.title: Fatigue across physical and mental health conditions: results from a multicenter study at the German Center for Mental Health.
studies.authors: Erschens, R, Zipfel, S, Schröpel, C, Adam, S H et al.
studies.abstract: Fatigue is a frequent and disabling symptom across many physical and mental health conditions. Despite similar phenomenology, research has largely focused on single conditions using heterogeneous assessments, limiting cross-condition comparability. This study examines fatigue-related symptom burden across diverse clinical conditions within a shared framework. In this multicenter cross-sectional study, adult outpatients (18-65 years) were recruited at five German university hospitals into seven cohorts: chronic primary pain, multiple sclerosis, cancer, chronic renal failure, inflammatory bowel disease, post-COVID condition, and chronic fatigue syndrome. Fatigue was assessed using established self-report measures, including the Fatigue Severity Scale and the Chalder Fatigue Scale, alongside mental health measures. Group differences were analyzed using ANOVA and chi-square tests with adjusted post hoc comparisons. A total of 538 patients were included. Fatigue burden varied substantially across cohorts, with a largely consistent pattern across assessment instruments. Despite significant overall between-cohort differences, the post-COVID (n = 91), chronic primary pain (n = 110), and cancer (n = 124) cohorts showed comparable fatigue levels across several assessment instruments. Multiple sclerosis (n = 63) showed intermediate levels, whereas inflammatory bowel disease (n = 95) consistently showed the lowest fatigue burden. Due to the small sample size, chronic renal failure (n = 30) and chronic fatigue syndrome (n = 25) were analyzed descriptively. Across cohorts, fatigue and most psychological and somatic symptom measures were elevated relative to population reference values. Using a harmonized assessment framework across seven diagnostic cohorts, this study demonstrates meaningful differences in fatigue burden, with convergent patterns across instruments. The findings provide a reference for contextualizing fatigue severity across conditions and support future hypothesis-driven and mechanistic analyses.

studies.title: Rehabilitative efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy-based intervention for chronic fatigue syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
studies.authors: Jiang, Xiaoyu, Liu, Junnan, Li, Shulun, Pei, Qian et al.
studies.abstract: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) has been used for chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS), but previous studies have shown inconsistencies and divergent long-term outcomes. This study aims to assess the effectiveness of CBT in improving fatigue, physical functioning, and psychological health in patients with CFS. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from their inception to March 2025. Studies designed as randomized controlled trials, enrolling patients diagnosed with CFS who received CBT as a treatment intervention delivered face-to-face, in groups, or online were included. The primary outcome was the fatigue score, and the secondary outcomes were the physical function score, psychological outcomes, and adverse events. The quality of the included studies was evaluated using the Cochrane Assessment Tool for Risk of Bias Version 2 (RoB 2; The Cochrane Collaboration). Heterogeneity was detected by subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis. Fifteen randomized controlled trials with 2270 participants were involved. Meta-analysis demonstrated that CBT yielded significant posttreatment improvements across key outcomes. Fatigue severity was notably reduced, as measured by the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.44, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.57--0.32) and the Checklist Individual Strength (SMD = -0.88, 95% CI: -1.16--0.60). Physical functioning (physical function subscale of the Short Form Health Survey-36) subscale also improved significantly (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.23-0.41). Psychological health benefits were evident through reduced Symptom Checklist 90 (SMD = -0.44, 95% CI: -0.62--0.26) and specific decreases in anxiety (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-anxiety scale: SMD = -0.28, 95% CI: -0.46--0.10) and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-depression scale: SMD = -0.27, 95% CI: -0.45--0.09). Follow-up analyses confirmed sustained benefits: short-term (≤ 6 months) showed continued fatigue reduction (Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire: SMD = -0.29, 95% CI: -0.55--0.03) and improved physical function (physical function subscale of the Short Form Health Survey-36: SMD = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.03-0.58); long-term (6-24 months) maintained fatigue relief (SMD = -0.35, 95% CI: -0.50--0.19) and functional gains (SMD = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.06-0.37). Safety analysis showed no statistically significant difference in adverse event rates (odds ratio = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.36-1.01, P = .060). Based on our results, CBT may be an effective option for CFS, but further research is warranted.

studies.title: Making recovery conceivable: perspectives from healthcare professionals using psychologically and behaviourally informed approaches to chronic fatigue syndrome.
studies.journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being
studies.authors: Bakken, Anne Karen, Mengshoel, Anne Marit, Synnes, Oddgeir
studies.abstract: Healthcare professionals (HCPs) treating patients with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) work within a contested field marked by uncertainty. This study explored how HCPs using psychologically and behaviourally informed approaches to CFS understood therapeutic change and their role in facilitating recovery. We used reflexive thematic analysis of two focus groups and three individual interviews with 16 HCPs from five professions, purposively sampled across clinical settings. Participants had at least two years' experience working with patients with CFS and represented diverse therapeutic and theoretical perspectives. The analysis was organised around four interrelated themes: (1) meeting patients in a "no-man's-land", (2) offering a new explanatory "map", (3) navigating by the map, and (4) maintaining trust in a contested field. HCPs described offering frameworks integrating biological, psychological, and social processes. Two overlapping orientations emphasised either stress, overload, and impaired regulation or maladaptive learning, perception, and self-sustaining symptom processes. Across orientations, validation and fostering agency were central. Embodied experiences of improvement were considered important for strengthening trust and confidence that change was possible. Competing illness narratives challenged trust. Participating HCPs described explanatory frameworks, their application in practice, therapeutic relationships, and patients' embodied experiences of improvement as interacting to make recovery conceivable.

studies.title: Exploratory clinical and immunological changes following Tixagevimab/Cilgavimab administration in immunodeficient patients with SARS-CoV-2-associated ME/CFS and persistent circulating spike protein.
studies.authors: Seidel, Maximilian, Anft, Moritz, Wiemers, Lea, Seibert, Felix S et al.
studies.abstract: Persistent circulating SARS-CoV-2 spike protein has been proposed as a potential contributor to long-COVID pathophysiology. Whether administration of spike-targeting monoclonal antibodies is followed by changes in spike protein concentrations, autonomic receptor autoantibodies, or clinical outcomes remains uncertain. In this prospective, non-randomized observational study, 21 participants were enrolled. Ten immunodeficient patients with long-COVID-associated ME/CFS and detectable circulating spike protein received Tixagevimab/Cilgavimab for SARS-CoV-2 pre-exposure prophylaxis. One patient subsequently withdrew consent, leaving nine patients for paired baseline and 30-day follow-up analyses. Eleven healthy individuals with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection but without long COVID provided descriptive reference data and were not considered an efficacy control group. β1-adrenergic receptor autoantibody concentrations decreased from 26.8 ± 18.2 to 21.2 ± 14.7 U/ml (unadjusted p = 0.003). No statistically significant changes were observed for β2-adrenergic or M3/M4-muscarinic receptor autoantibodies. Median spike protein concentrations changed from 63 pg/ml (IQR 9-127) to 26 pg/ml (IQR 10-120; p = 0.63), with individual decreases observed in five of nine patients. None of the assessed clinical outcomes changed significantly at group level. Changes in spike protein concentrations were not significantly correlated with changes in the assessed autonomic receptor autoantibodies. Tixagevimab/Cilgavimab administration was followed by a nominally significant within-patient reduction in β1-adrenergic receptor autoantibody concentrations, but not by conclusive changes in circulating spike protein or clinical outcomes. These findings are preliminary and hypothesis-generating. The small sample size, non-randomized design, brief 30-day follow-up, inclusion of only immunodeficient patients, and absence of an untreated disease-matched control group preclude conclusions regarding therapeutic efficacy.

studies.title: Characterizing Pediatric Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Symptom Burden, Functional Impairment, and Comparison with Adults in the Multisite Clinical Assessment of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Study.
studies.authors: Weaver, Stephanie Sargent, Regan, Joanna J, Issa, Anindita, Fall, Elizabeth A et al.
studies.abstract: To characterize the clinical, functional, and educational characteristics of adolescents with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and compare selected illness domains with adults in the Multi-Site Clinical Assessment of ME/CFS (MCAM) study. Baseline cross-sectional data from adolescents aged 10-17 years enrolled in MCAM were analyzed. Standardized measures included the Short Form-36, CDC Symptom Inventory, Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory, and selected domains of the DePaul Questionnaire. Descriptive statistics characterized the pediatric cohort and bivariate analyses compared adolescents with adults enrolled in MCAM. Forty adolescents (mean age, 15.3 years; 52.5% female) were included. Mean illness duration was 4.0 years. Educational disruption was substantial: 64% received homebound or homeschool instruction, 89% missed school because of illness, and participants missed a mean of 10.8 school days during the preceding month. Physical health-related quality of life was substantially impaired. Persistent postexertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, fatigue, and neurocognitive symptoms were common. Compared with adults (n = 595), adolescents had shorter illness duration and better physical functioning, vitality, and social functioning, whereas mental health scores were similar. Adults reported greater burden across several physical symptom domains, although many between-group differences were small. Adolescents with ME/CFS experience substantial multisystem symptom burden, impaired physical functioning, and educational disruption. Many core clinical features were similar to those in adults, supporting the need for early recognition and appropriate clinical and educational support.

studies.title: Patient's knowledge, doctor's ignorance: The production of knowledge about myalgic encephalomyelitis.
studies.journal: Studies in history and philosophy of science
studies.authors: de Canson, Chloé
studies.abstract: It is usually assumed that patient and doctor know strictly different things: the patient knows the phenomenological aspects of their illness, and the doctor knows its medical aspects. I present a case study, that of myalgic encephalomyelitis, wherein, due to severely dysfunctional institutional knowledge production and transmission mechanisms, the medical aspects of the illness are on the whole better understood by sick people than by their doctors. Indeed, lay scientists within the patient community disseminate and produce science on their disease, ensuring that patients as a whole have reliable knowledge about their disease. By contrast, systemically produced and systemically maintained ignorance on the part of medical professionals is the norm, and may be beyond the specific case study I present.

studies.title: "If I Accomplish Nothing Else but Hope, That Will be Enough": The Ethics and Morality of Market-Based Hope in Illness Entrepreneurship.
studies.authors: Geiger, Susi, Loza, Olya
studies.abstract: How do entrepreneurs embody and enact hope as a motor for ethical agency-agency that builds one's own and others' capacities and capabilities to overcome a painful present? This study puts hope at the center of theorizing around the activities of entrepreneurs who leverage it both as a way to sketch a new life for themselves and to sell it to others. Through the case of illness entrepreneurs-recovery coaches for those suffering from chronic illnesses-we observe the moral struggles involved when hope becomes framed within the logic of the market. Recovery coaches at once embody hope (as formerly sick people who have recovered), neatly package and sell it (as entrepreneurs), and manifest it (opening up new spaces of possibility for themselves). The work involved in balancing these threads requires constant realignment of the entrepreneurs' own hopes for a new life and their care for others. We show how, through these moral struggles, hope opens up new spaces of possibility and imbues people-both entrepreneurs and their clients-with the agency to move toward those new horizons. Conceptualizing the complex entanglements of hope, care, and ethical agency, our study represents a foray into recent calls for assembling and theorizing the 'architecture of hope' in organization and entrepreneurship studies. We also discuss whether this entrepreneurship, balancing hope and care to enable ethical agency, opens up new ways of understanding morality and agency in market contexts.

studies.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
studies.authors: Gultekin, Kadir, Bartels, Jennifer L, Cardenas, Carlos E, Kumar, Yogesh et al.
